customer_impact_description: AuroraPay e-Transfer unavailable for most participants during early afternoon peak; customers unable to send or receive money.
Intermittent timeouts and slow responses for AuroraPay Debit authorizations at select merchants; some customers forced to retry or use alternate payment methods.
Elevated losses from a targeted impersonation scam campaign where fraudsters convinced customers to send e-Transfers to fraudulent accounts.
Cluster of account takeover events exploiting reused credentials on a subset of participants; abnormal login patterns and rapid outgoing transfers observed.
Discovery of a legacy admin group with broad privileges remaining active in a core AuroraPay configuration service; no confirmed misuse but elevated risk exposure.
Quarterly privileged access review for two key components was delayed and performed with limited challenge, leaving stale access in place for several weeks.
Outage at a critical fraud analytics vendor forced AuroraPay to operate on fallback rule sets with reduced detection capability for approximately 45 minutes.
Notification to oversight body regarding the 15 Feb e-Transfer outage (INC1) was submitted later than internal expectations and lacked complete root cause detail in the initial communication.
